pool.prompt: Match each wavelength to its primary use in OSP or fiber networks.

targets.label: GPON upstream + standard short-reach SMF transceivers

pool.explanation: 850 nm: multimode short-reach. 1310 nm: O-band, GPON upstream, LR/LX SMF transceivers. 1550 nm: C-band, lowest loss, long-haul/DWDM. 1625 nm: L-band diagnostic, macrobend hunting on in-service fibers.
pool.citation: ITU-T G.652; ITU-T G.984 (GPON); OTDR best practice (FOA Reference Guide).

pool.prompt: A technician is doing an OTDR trace on a live GPON fiber to locate a suspected macrobend. Which wavelength should they use, and why?
choices: 1310 nm, because it matches the GPON upstream wavelength and will show the bend clearly
1490 nm, to match the GPON downstream signal
1625 nm, because it exaggerates macrobend loss and is outside the GPON signal wavelengths — it can be injected without interrupting service
850 nm, because it has the highest sensitivity in the O-band
pool.explanation: 1625 nm is outside the 1310/1490 nm GPON signal bands. With appropriate WDM filters, a 1625 nm OTDR pulse can be injected without interfering with live traffic, and macrobend loss grows with wavelength, so 1625 nm shows the bend more clearly.
pool.fieldNote: Check that the fiber's WDM filter system actually supports 1625 nm pass-through before injecting — some older PON filter designs block wavelengths above 1610 nm.

pool.prompt: CWDM uses 20 nm channel spacing; DWDM uses 0.8 nm (or tighter) channel spacing. What is the key consequence of this difference for field crews?
choices: CWDM requires armored cable; DWDM can use standard OSP cable

DWDM requires much more precise laser wavelength stability and end-face cleanliness — including APC connectors — because the channels are so close together that small reflections can desensitize the narrow-linewidth lasers
CWDM can use multimode fiber; DWDM requires single-mode
There is no field implication — the spacing only matters to the system designer
pool.explanation: DWDM channels are 0.4-0.8 nm apart. A back-reflection negligible on a standard SMF link can degrade a DWDM system's narrow-linewidth lasers. APC connectors (>=60 dB ORL) are standard practice on DWDM routes for this reason.
pool.fieldNote: On a DWDM installation, end-face inspection with an IEC 61300-3-35 compliant scope is not optional — a single dirty APC connector can take down multiple 100G channels simultaneously.

pool.prompt: What is the ITU-T standard number and channel spacing for CWDM, and how does it compare to DWDM?
choices: ITU-T G.694.2, 20 nm spacing (18 wavelengths, 1270-1610 nm) — much wider than DWDM's 0.4-0.8 nm spacing under G.694.1
ITU-T G.694.1, 0.8 nm spacing — identical to DWDM
ITU-T G.652, 100 nm spacing — wider than both CWDM and DWDM combined
There is no ITU-T standard for CWDM channel spacing
pool.explanation: ITU-T G.694.2 defines CWDM's 18 wavelengths spanning 1270-1610 nm at 20 nm spacing — wide enough to use uncooled lasers, unlike DWDM (G.694.1), which packs channels at 0.8 nm (100 GHz) or 0.4 nm (50 GHz) spacing within the C-band.

pool.prompt: Why does DWDM require thermoelectric-cooled (TEC) lasers while CWDM typically uses uncooled lasers?
choices: TEC lasers are simply more expensive and offer no functional benefit for DWDM

DWDM's tight 0.4-0.8 nm channel spacing requires holding wavelength within roughly +/-0.1 nm to avoid adjacent-channel interference; CWDM's 20 nm spacing gives enough margin that uncooled lasers (whose wavelength drifts with temperature) are acceptable
CWDM lasers physically cannot be cooled due to their wavelength range
TEC cooling is required by OSHA for all long-haul optical equipment
pool.explanation: Laser wavelength drifts with temperature. DWDM's narrow channel spacing leaves very little room for drift before a channel bleeds into its neighbor, so temperature stabilization (TEC) is required. CWDM's much wider 20 nm spacing tolerates the wavelength drift of an uncooled laser.

pool.prompt: What OSP-relevant standard governs the GPON downstream/upstream wavelength plan (1490/1310 nm) that a field crew must avoid interfering with when injecting an OTDR test pulse?
choices: ITU-T G.984 (GPON)
ITU-T G.652 (fiber cable characteristics only, not wavelength plan)
NESC C2-2023
IEEE 802.3
pool.explanation: ITU-T G.984 is the GPON standard, defining the downstream (1490 nm)/upstream (1310 nm) wavelength plan that WDM filters at each end must isolate from a diagnostic OTDR test injected at a separate wavelength like 1625 nm.

pool.prompt: A DWDM route shows unexplained signal degradation across multiple 100G channels simultaneously. What field cause is a strong first suspect, given DWDM's sensitivity to connector quality?
choices: A single connector at any point on the shared optical path being dirty or improperly cleaned, since DWDM's tight channel spacing amplifies the impact of back-reflection from a single bad interface
The fiber's core diameter shrinking over time
A software bug in the DWDM multiplexer with no physical-layer cause
Ambient humidity affecting the glass's index of refraction
pool.explanation: Because all DWDM channels share the same physical fiber path and connectors, a single dirty or damaged connector — which might be a minor annoyance on a single-wavelength link — can desensitize the narrow-linewidth lasers across every channel riding that connector, explaining a multi-channel degradation.

pool.prompt: Which wavelength window sits within the C-band and is the standard choice for both lowest-attenuation long-haul transmission AND DWDM systems?
choices: 850 nm
pool.explanation: 1550 nm falls within the C-band (roughly 1530-1565 nm), which combines the fiber's lowest attenuation window with the wavelength range where DWDM systems concentrate their channels — making it the natural choice for long-haul and DWDM applications.
